title: Pre-Analysis — Thrust Lever Detent Seal and Friction Clamp Standard
abstract: Re-analysis of the detent seal and friction clamp standard, opened when the measurement bulletin produced a larger population than expected, covering exchange capacity, the measurement gate and the crew limitation.

sections.objective: The breakout force measurement bulletin returned readings below the acceptance band on far more aircraft than the fleet model predicted. The round was opened to establish whether the acceptance band was right, whether the exchange quadrant supply could carry the resulting demand, and what the operators should be told in the meantime.
sections.findings_summary: Four items were confirmed and the band was left unchanged. The measurement bulletin is the gate for the exchange bulletin and the two are correctly coupled; the larger population is a real finding about the fleet and not an artefact of the measurement. The exchange bulletin ships quadrants set up on the bench, which is what makes the eighteen week lead time the binding constraint rather than the shop capacity. The parts figure states that individual replacement of the detent seal on the aircraft is not permitted, which closes off the obvious workaround. The fourth finding is the crew limitation, which already tells crews to confirm the lever position visually where the tactile step is unclear, and which turns out to be the mitigation the fleet has been running on without anybody recording it as such.
sections.next_steps: Leave the acceptance band unchanged and publish the population figure so that operators can plan. Confirm the exchange quadrant lead time with the supplier and prioritise aircraft with readings furthest below the band. Record the crew limitation explicitly as the interim mitigation.

evidence.similarity_note: The crew limitation is written about lever position and gate markings; the modification text is about a fluorosilicone seal and a bonded clamp face. No identifier is shared and the registers are entirely different.
